title: Opening remarks + quick Q&A crib for small group bridge session (scratch)
content:
Purpose: scratch notes for a short (~15 min) leadership bridge session with ~40 engineers across infra + serving runtime. Goal = reassure, give top-level course, quick Q&A. This is intentionally short-form — meant for use in a stand-up style drop-in (not the full all-hands).

Context notes (very quick):
- Recent capacity blips last week (brief outage + elevated latency regionally). Ops postmortem in progress — SRE/infra drafting timeline.
- Dedicated pilot onboarding next month — customers excited but ops will tighten runbooks.
- Product shipped smaller Optimize alpha; early metrics promising but we need to watch backend CPU footprint.

Audience: engineers (mid-senior), oncall, a few product managers. Keep it practical, avoid high-level marketing language.

Opening (1.5 - 2 min):
- Quick hello + why we’re here: "Hi all — I’m Avery. I’ll keep this short: two quick updates + one ask + 5 minutes for questions."
- Tone: calm, factual, ownership.

Update 1 — Reliability snapshot (2 min):
- What happened: transient capacity stress on west-2 (GPU eviction cascade) — affected ~6% of requests for ~18 minutes during morning spike.
- Immediate mitigation: emergency scaling policy triggered, fallback routing engaged, degraded but available for most customers.
- Where we are now: primary mitigations in place; SLOs recovering; full timeline + RCA will land in the SRE folder later today.
- Ask from engs: keep an eye on memory/KV cache growth signals in dashboards; if you see unexpected spikes tag SRE channel and paste graph link.

Update 2 — Pilot & product (2 min):
- Dedicated pilot onboarding: first customer test in 3 weeks. We’re running a dry-run next Tue with canary traffic in staging.
- Impact: small infra config tweaks, extended autoscaler stress tests, docs for customer handoff (ops + solutions).
- Ask: owners for the next two weeks (infra: Rowan; solutions: Marta) — expect pings for short pairing sessions.

Micro ask (30s):
- If you’re deep in serving-runtime or batching flow, please RSVP to a 30-minute dry-run on Tue 10–10:30am (calendar invite follows). We need at least 5 engineers to simulate sustained small-burst traffic.

Q&A crib (for CM to read if needed) — likely questions + short answers:
- Q: "Are customer requests impacted?"
  A: "Short blip for a subset; no data loss; we served degraded but available. Customers on Dedicated had automated fallbacks. We’ll share customer-facing comms only after we validate the RCA."
- Q: "Was this human error or system failure?"
  A: "Too early to assign cause. Initial symptoms point to a coupling between cache expiry and autoscaler heuristics; RCA will clarify."
- Q: "Is our SLO at risk?"
  A: "Not long-term. We saw a temporary dip but SLO burn is within alerting thresholds and we’re on a recovery trajectory. We’ll surface if it changes."
- Q: "Will this delay the Dedicated pilot?"
  A: "No. Pilot timeline stands; added mitigations are on the critical path but not blocking. We’re running dry-run tests to validate."

Rehearsal cues / script snippets (for handoff to speaker):
- "I’ll be brief :) — two quick updates and one ask. First, reliability: last Tuesday we saw a short capacity stress in west-2. We responded with emergency scaling and routing fallbacks; customers remained served though latency was elevated for a subset. The SRE team has immediate mitigations in place and an RCA will be posted today."
- Pause (2s)
- "Second: pilot & dry-run — we’re green to proceed but we need help simulating steady small-burst traffic in staging next week. Look for the calendar invite, please RSVP."

Slack/Comms follow-up plan (notes):
- Post short summary to #eng-all within 1 hour of drop-in. Include links: incident stub, staging dry-run invite, call-to-action for volunteers.
- Draft customer-facing line (ops/customer-success will approve): one-liner acknowledging brief disruption, no data loss, RCA forthcoming. Don’t send until SRE thumbs-up.

Open questions / TODOs (quick list):
- [ ] Confirm who will paste the incident stub to #eng-all (assign: Marta?)
- [ ] Draft staging test runbook (assign: Rowan)
- [ ] Confirm dry-run engineer list + calendar invite by EOD Monday (owner: Avery)
- [ ] Pre-draft customer-facing ack for CS review (owner: Marta)

Backup detail (if asked for deeper technical color):
- Observed: KV cache retention spikes at ~t0+3min after traffic surge; autoscaler heuristics misinterpreted resource signals and scaled down before cache cold start complete. This created a feedback loop.
- Short-term fix: increase autoscaler cooldown and add a spacing window for cache rehydration; long-term: tune heuristics and add a KV health signal.

Tone/phrasing reminders (meta):
- No absolutes (avoid "never" / "always"); use "probable/initial/likely" until RCA is complete.
- Empathy for oncall: name the response teams and thank them.
- Keep customer-facing language conservative: facts + reassurance + next step.

Notes to self (Avery):
- Run 1 quick rehearsal today 4pm with Marta. Keep it under 10 minutes.
- Bring one slide: timeline graphic (3 bullets) + 1 CTA. Simple.

Rough script end (15s):
- "Thanks — we’ll keep this short. If you have follow-ups, ping me or drop questions in the doc; Marta and Rowan will be coordinating dry-run logistics. Back to your day."

— end of scratch. Keep this doc as ephemeral working copy; final copy to be moved to shared_drives/internal-comm when polished.
